uncertainties: Mesopotamian middle chronology used throughout (Hammurabi 1792-1750, Babylon falls to Mursili I in 1595).
Corded Ware is coloured 'steppe' to render the Indo-European expansion story; it is equally ancestral to Germanic/Baltic/Slavic worlds, so the -2500 north reads more 'steppe' than some would like.
Bell Beaker is shown as one network entity from the Tagus to Britain (family 'celtic' as shorthand for the Atlantic facade's later trajectory); its Iberian core was likely non-Indo-European.
Unetice/Tumulus/Urnfield are tagged 'celtic' following the conventional proto-Celtic reading of the Urnfield-Hallstatt line; this is contested for Unetice especially.
Trzciniec and Lusatian are tagged 'baltic' as 'proto-Balto-Slavic'; their ethnolinguistic identity is genuinely unresolved (Lusatian is sometimes read as Venetic or pre-Germanic).
Balkan Bronze communities are tagged 'paleo_balkan' from -2500 (anticipating Thracian/Illyrian ethnogenesis); the split into proto-Illyrians/proto-Thracians at -1300 is conventional, not documentary.
Italy switches to 'italic' at -1450 with the Terramare, per the majority view that Italic speakers were then established in the Po plain; dates from -1700 to -1200 are defended in the literature.
Thera eruption placed at the -1600 slice (radiocarbon c. 1620-1600 BC); the traditional archaeological date is c. 1530-1500 BC.

Crete assigned to Mycenaeans at -1450: LM IB destructions and the Knossos takeover fall c. 1470-1450, so the handover is shown at its earliest defensible moment; Minoans as an entity end here though the population remained largely 'Minoan'.
Mitanni at -1450 is given MES_N (Assur as vassal), ARM_W (Isuwa orbit) and CIL (Kizzuwatna client, flagged contested); all three were spheres of influence rather than provinces.
PON is Hittite until -1450, then Kaska: Kaska first appear in texts in the 15th century already holding Nerik, so their earlier presence is likely but undocumented.
CON (Bosphorus) is grouped with Troy/Wilusa in the LBA for geographic convenience; there is no evidence of Trojan political control of the European shore.
Alashiya is treated as a single kingdom covering all Cyprus with capital Enkomi; scholarship is divided on whether it covered the whole island (capital possibly Kalavasos).
El Argar is typed as a state from -2000 ('arguably western Europe's first state'); many prefer 'complex chiefdom'. Its collapse (c. 1550) shows as final crisis at -1600.
Sumerians are placed in the 'semitic_levantine' family bucket (the spec's Mesopotamian family) despite Sumerian being non-Semitic; cultureName distinguishes them.

Population figures are order-of-magnitude interpolations from McEvedy & Jones-style series, Butzer's Egypt estimates (1-3M) and survey-based Aegean figures; culture/tribal entities count in-map population only. Overall map total grows from c. 11M at -3000 to c. 20M at -1300, dipping after.
Egypt at -1200 keeps LEV (Merneptah's stele shows active control), flagged contested; the withdrawal happens in the next era's first slice.

WebSearch-verified facts (all confirmed the draft, one correction made): Ur's fall to Elam is firmly 2004 BC (matches the -2000 slice exactly); Thera's radiocarbon/archaeological dating gap (c.1600 vs c.1500 BC) is a live, unresolved controversy, not settled either way; the Mycenaean takeover of Knossos and start of Linear B is standardly dated c. 1450 BC (matches the brief's instruction and this file's -1450 slice); Tukulti-Ninurta I's sack of Babylon is c. 1225 BC (consistent with 'shaken, recovering' Babylon at -1200); Adad-nirari I (1305-1274 BC) did conquer/vassalize Mitanni and take the 'great king' title, matching the -1300 slice; Shamshi-Adad I's reign (c. 1809-1776 BC) matches his 'Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia' shown at -1800; the Merneptah Stele/Battle of Perire date of 1208 BC matches the -1200 slice's Libyan-war event. One correction: Arzawa's earliest attestation is Hattusili I's raid c. 1650 BC (not c. 1700 BC as originally drafted), so its 'founded' year was moved to -1650. Kaska sources disagree on their earliest textual appearance (Hantili I c. 1590s vs Hantili II prayers c. 1450 BC holding Nerik already); this file keeps them off-map until -1450 as the more conservative reading, per the existing uncertainty above.
